lastCompletedStory.title: Close the CREATE-on-main worktree-coherence invariant for absent paths

nextStoryContext: US-001 (CAM-140) was already ~90% closed by prior work: CAM-142 (PR #106) already added `syncWorktreeIfOnMain(cwd, [filename], spawnFn)` inside writeIssueFile's CREATE-route success block (src/issues/alloc.ts:199) and shipped test/integration/write-issue-file-worktree-sync.test.ts (AC1). CAM-137 already shipped test/integration/sync-worktree-on-main.test.ts covering ADD/MODIFY/DELETE/REGRESSION via commitTreeToMain. This story's only remaining gap was AC3: a DIRECT function-level test of syncWorktreeIfOnMain (not routed through commitTreeToMain) proving it MATERIALIZES a path absent from the worktree (staged deletion via `git rm`), not merely staged-restores a path already present, plus an off-main inert-call assertion in the same test. Added one new test case to test/integration/sync-worktree-on-main.test.ts (no production code changes -- src/git/on-main.ts's syncWorktreeIfOnMain was already correct per CAM-137). No further work needed on this invariant unless a new on-main writer is added without reusing syncWorktreeIfOnMain/commitTreeToMain.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed `git restore --staged --worktree --source=<tree> -- <pathspec>` creates the path in both index and worktree when absent from both but present in the source tree (docs state the inverse explicitly: a tracked path absent from the restore source is removed to match). This matches syncWorktreeIfOnMain's contract and the new AC3 direct-materialization regression test.
